# Options may appear anywhere on the command line, GNU style: before, after
# or between targets and var=value assignments. "--" ends option parsing.

# a flag after the target
mk -p 1 b -n
stdout '^b: echo built b$'
! stdout '^built'

# flags between targets, and a flag with a value after them
mk a -n b -f mkfile
stdout '^a: echo built a$'
stdout '^b: echo built b$'
! stdout '^built'

# an assignment among flags and targets
mk v -p 1 NAME=x -n
stdout '^v: echo value x$'

# after --, everything is a target, even if it looks like a flag
mk -p 1 -- -odd
stdout '^built -odd$'
! mk -p 1 -- b -n
stderr 'don''t know how to make -n'

-- mkfile --
a b:V:
	echo built $target

NAME = default
v:V:
	echo value $NAME

-odd:V:
	echo built $target
